title: Singleton probability bound
statement: Fix a positive integer $n$, a deterministic disjointness protocol $p$ on length-$n$ inputs, a real number $\gamma$, and an achievable statistic $z$. If the total variation distance between the conditional law of the special-coordinate bit pair given $z$ and the uniform law on $\{0,1\}^2$ is at most $2\gamma$, then for every bit pair $b\in\{0,1\}^2$, the absolute difference between its probability under that conditional law and $1/4$ is at most $2\gamma$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a deterministic disjointness protocol on length-$n$ inputs
The total variation distance of the conditional special-pair law from uniform is at most $2\gamma$
replaced:
Fix a positive integer $n$ and a deterministic communication protocol $p$ for the
disjointness problem on inputs of length $n$, drawn under the hard distribution. Write
$(x_T, y_T)$ for the pair of Alice's and Bob's bits at the special coordinate $T$, and
for a value $z$ of the conditioning statistic let $\mu_z$ denote the conditional law of
this bit-pair on $\{0,1\}^2$ given that the statistic equals $z$. Suppose $z$ is
$\gamma$-good, in the sense that the total variation distance between $\mu_z$ and the
uniform distribution on $\{0,1\}^2$ is at most $2\gamma$. Then for every bit-pair $b \in
\{0,1\}^2$,
\[
  \abs{\mu_z(\{b\}) - \tfrac{1}{4}} \le 2\gamma .
\]
